background:
Ephesians: The Letter, Its World and Your Notes

Study notes · dates are approximate and scholars vary

At a glance

Ephesians was most likely written around AD 60–62, by Paul under house arrest in Rome, while Nero ruled the empire.

QuestionTraditional viewNotes
AuthorThe apostle Paul (Eph 1:1; 3:1)Some modern scholars think a follower of Paul wrote it around AD 80–90; most conservative and many mainstream scholars hold to Paul.
DateAbout AD 60–62Some place it earlier, during an imprisonment in Caesarea (AD 57–59).
Written fromRome, under house arrest (Acts 28:16, 30)Paul calls himself “the prisoner” (3:1; 4:1) and “an ambassador in chains” (6:20).
Carried byTychicus (Eph 6:21–22)The same messenger as Colossians and likely Philemon; the three letters traveled together.
Written toBelievers in Ephesus and likely the wider province of Asia“At Ephesus” is missing from some of the oldest manuscripts, so it may have been a circular letter.
Roman emperorNero (ruled AD 54–68)The letter predates his persecution of Christians after the fire of AD 64.

The “Prison Letters” (Ephesians, Philippians, Colossians and Philemon) all come from this same period of Paul's life.

Paul's road to Ephesians

Paul had spent nearly three years in Ephesus, so he wrote to people he knew well. Dates are approximate; scholars vary by a year or two.

Rome under Nero (AD 60–62)

Paul wrote just as Nero's reign was turning from its stable early years toward the cruelty it is remembered for. AD 62 was a turning point.

  • The “good years” end. Nero's early rule (AD 54–59) was steered by his tutor, the Stoic philosopher Seneca, and the guard prefect Burrus. Nero had his own mother, Agrippina, killed in AD 59.
  • AD 62, a dark year. Burrus died, possibly poisoned. Seneca withdrew from court. Nero divorced and then had his wife Octavia killed, and married Poppaea Sabina. Treason trials returned.
  • Tigellinus rises. The ruthless Tigellinus became guard prefect in AD 62 and fed Nero's paranoia.
  • Seneca's writing. In retirement (AD 62–65) Seneca wrote his Moral Letters, a classic of Stoic ethics, an interesting comparison with Ephesians 4–5.
  • Literature. Pliny the Elder was gathering material for his Natural History; the poet Lucan and the satirist Petronius were at Nero's court.
  • Earthquake at Pompeii. In AD 62 (or 63) a strong earthquake damaged Pompeii and Herculaneum, 17 years before Vesuvius buried them.
  • What came next. The Great Fire of Rome in AD 64 led Nero to blame and execute Christians, the first state persecution. Ephesians was written in the quiet before that storm.

Rome itself had roughly a million people, perhaps a third of them slaves. Paul's instructions to masters and slaves (6:5–9) addressed the everyday reality of his readers.

The city of Ephesus

Ephesus was one of the great cities of the empire, the leading city of the Roman province of Asia (western Türkiye today), with perhaps 200,000–250,000 people.

  • Temple of Artemis. The Artemision was one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World, about four times the size of the Parthenon. It also served as a major bank, and its worship drove the local economy (Acts 19:24–27).
  • Port and trade. A harbor on the Aegean linked Ephesus to Rome, Egypt and the East. Silt from the Cayster River was already a problem and eventually left the ruins miles inland.
  • The great theater. It seated about 24,000 and is where the silversmiths' riot took place (Acts 19:29). It still stands.
  • Magic and the occult. Ephesus was famous for magic spells called the “Ephesian letters.” New believers burned scrolls of magic worth 50,000 silver coins (Acts 19:19), background for Paul's language about “powers” and “spiritual hosts” (1:21; 6:12).
  • Emperor worship. Ephesus held temples to Rome and the deified emperors. Calling Jesus “far above all rule, and authority” (1:21) was a bold claim in that setting.
  • A mixed church. Jews had lived in Ephesus for generations, with Roman protections for their worship. A church of Jews and Gentiles together explains Paul's focus on “the middle wall of partition” torn down (2:14).

The famous Library of Celsus seen in photos today was built later, about AD 110–135.

The time map

The shaded band marks AD 60–62. Within two years of the letter, Rome burned and Nero turned on Christians; within eight, Jerusalem's temple was gone.

Maps: then and now

Ephesus sat on the Aegean coast of the Roman province of Asia, at the hub of roads linking the cities Paul and John wrote to. Today the ruins lie in western Türkiye beside the town of Selçuk.

In Paul's day Ephesus had a harbor and Miletus sat on a gulf of the sea (Acts 20:15–17). Both were later left inland as rivers silted up their harbors, so the ancient shoreline shown is approximate.

Around the world, about AD 60–62

While Paul wrote from Rome, the empire was fighting on two frontiers, and great civilizations were flourishing far beyond its reach.

RegionWhat was happening
BritainBoudica's revolt (AD 60–61). The queen of the Iceni led a rebellion that burned London, Colchester and St Albans before Roman legions crushed it.
JudeaRising tension. Governor Festus died in office in AD 62. In the gap before his successor arrived, the high priest had James, the brother of Jesus, stoned, as Josephus records. The Jewish revolt broke out in AD 66.
Armenia and ParthiaRome's general Corbulo fought Parthia over control of Armenia, AD 58–63. A Roman army surrendered at Rhandeia in AD 62; a compromise peace followed in 63.
Germany and the DanubeLegions held the Rhine and Danube frontiers against Germanic tribes.
ChinaThe Eastern Han dynasty under Emperor Ming (AD 57–75), roughly as large and populous as Rome. Tradition says Buddhism reached China in his reign. Silk traveled west along trade routes to Rome.
India and Central AsiaThe Kushan Empire was forming across Afghanistan and northern India. Roman ships sailed to southern India for pepper and spices. Tradition holds the apostle Thomas went to India.
Arabia and AfricaThe Nabataean kingdom (capital Petra) controlled incense routes. The kingdom of Aksum (Ethiopia) was rising; Meroë (Sudan) was ruled by queens called Kandake, the “Candace” of Acts 8:27.
The AmericasTeotihuacan near modern Mexico City was growing into one of the world's largest cities. The Moche and Nazca cultures flourished in Peru.

How the setting shapes the study

Knowing the world around the letter brings several passages into sharper focus.

PassageConnection to the times
Eph 1:20–23Christ seated “far above all rule, and authority”: written to a city full of emperor temples, under an emperor who would soon be worshiped as divine.
Eph 2:11–22The “middle wall of partition”: the Jerusalem temple had a literal barrier warning Gentiles to stay out on pain of death. Paul was arrested over a charge of bringing a Gentile past it (Acts 21:28–29).
Eph 3:1; 4:1“The prisoner”: Paul was chained to a Roman guard as he wrote.
Eph 5:18“Be not drunken with wine”: drunken revelry was part of pagan festivals, including the cult of Dionysus.
Eph 5:22–6:9Household instructions follow the Roman “household code” pattern (husbands, children, slaves) but reshape it with mutual duties under Christ.
Eph 6:10–17The armor of God: Paul's guard wore this equipment daily in front of him.
Eph 6:12“Spiritual hosts of wickedness”: a direct word to a church that came out of Ephesian magic (Acts 19:18–19).

A generation later, Jesus' letter to Ephesus in Revelation 2:1–7 praises the church's endurance but warns that it had left its first love, a sobering follow-up to read alongside Ephesians.

items.text: Greeting
Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus through the will of God, to the saints that are at Ephesus, and the faithful in Christ Jesus:
Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
Every Spiritual Blessing in Christ
Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who hath blessed us with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places in Christ:
even as he chose us in him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and without blemish before him in love:
having foreordained us unto adoption as sons through Jesus Christ unto himself, according to the good pleasure of his will,
to the praise of the glory of his grace, which he freely bestowed on us in the Beloved:
in whom we have our redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of our trespasses, according to the riches of his grace,
which he made to abound toward us in all wisdom and prudence,
making known unto us the mystery of his will, according to his good pleasure which he purposed in him
unto a dispensation of the fulness of the times, to sum up all things in Christ, the things in the heavens, and the things upon the earth; in him, I say,
in whom also we were made a heritage, having been foreordained according to the purpose of him who worketh all things after the counsel of his will;
to the end that we should be unto the praise of his glory, we who had before hoped in Christ:
in whom ye also, having heard the word of the truth, the gospel of your salvation,—in whom, having also believed, ye were sealed with the Holy Spirit of promise,
which is an earnest of our inheritance, unto the redemption of God’s own possession, unto the praise of his glory.
Paul’s Prayer for Wisdom
For this cause I also, having heard of the faith in the Lord Jesus which is among you, and the love which ye show toward all the saints,
cease not to give thanks for you, making mention of you in my prayers;
that the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of glory, may give unto you a spirit of wisdom and revelation in the knowledge of him;
having the eyes of your heart enlightened, that ye may know what is the hope of his calling, what the riches of the glory of his inheritance in the saints,
and what the exceeding greatness of his power to us-ward who believe, according to that working of the strength of his might
which he wrought in Christ, when he raised him from the dead, and made him to sit at his right hand in the heavenly places,
far above all rule, and authority, and power, and dominion, and every name that is named, not only in this world, but also in that which is to come:
and he put all things in subjection under his feet, and gave him to be head over all things to the church,
which is his body, the fulness of him that filleth all in all.

summary.title: CHAPTER 1 IN SUMMARY
paras: Paul opens with a burst of praise for every spiritual blessing believers have “in Christ.” God chose them before the foundation of the world, adopted them as His sons, redeemed and forgave them through Christ’s blood, and sealed them with the Holy Spirit as a pledge of the inheritance still to come. Every part of it flows from God’s will and grace, and every part of it is “unto the praise of his glory.” Behind it all stands God’s great plan to sum up all things in Christ.

Paul then prays that the Ephesians would truly grasp what they already have: the hope of God’s calling, the riches of His inheritance in the saints, and the surpassing greatness of His power toward those who believe. That is the same power that raised Christ from the dead and seated Him far above every ruler, authority and name. And this exalted Christ has been given as head over all things to the church, which is His body.

items.text: Made Alive by Grace
And you did he make alive, when ye were dead through your trespasses and sins,
wherein ye once walked according to the course of this world, according to the prince of the powers of the air, of the spirit that now worketh in the sons of disobedience;
among whom we also all once lived in the lusts of our flesh, doing the desires of the flesh and of the mind, and were by nature children of wrath, even as the rest:—
but God, being rich in mercy, for his great love wherewith he loved us,
even when we were dead through our trespasses, made us alive together with Christ (by grace have ye been saved),
and raised us up with him, and made us to sit with him in the heavenly places, in Christ Jesus:
that in the ages to come he might show the exceeding riches of his grace in kindness toward us in Christ Jesus:
for by grace have ye been saved through faith; and that not of yourselves, it is the gift of God;
not of works, that no man should glory.
For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God afore prepared that we should walk in them.
One New People in Christ
Wherefore remember, that once ye, the Gentiles in the flesh, who are called Uncircumcision by that which is called Circumcision, in the flesh, made by hands;
that ye were at that time separate from Christ, alienated from the commonwealth of Israel, and strangers from the covenants of the promise, having no hope and without God in the world.
But now in Christ Jesus ye that once were far off are made nigh in the blood of Christ.
For he is our peace, who made both one, and brake down the middle wall of partition,
having abolished in his flesh the enmity, even the law of commandments contained in ordinances; that he might create in himself of the two one new man, so making peace;
and might reconcile them both in one body unto God through the cross, having slain the enmity thereby:
and he came and preached peace to you that were far off, and peace to them that were nigh:
for through him we both have our access in one Spirit unto the Father.
So then ye are no more strangers and sojourners, but ye are fellow-citizens with the saints, and of the household of God,
being built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Christ Jesus himself being the chief corner stone;
in whom each several building, fitly framed together, groweth into a holy temple in the Lord;
in whom ye also are builded together for a habitation of God in the Spirit.

summary.title: CHAPTER 2 IN SUMMARY
paras: Paul reminds his readers what they were before Christ: dead in trespasses and sins, following the course of this world and “the prince of the powers of the air,” by nature children of wrath. “But God, being rich in mercy” made them alive together with Christ and seated them with Him in the heavenly places. Salvation is by grace through faith, the gift of God and not of works, so no one can boast. Yet it produces good works that God prepared for His people to walk in.

The second half turns to Jew and Gentile. Gentiles were once far off, without Christ, without hope and without God in the world, but now they have been brought near by Christ’s blood. Christ Himself is our peace: He broke down the dividing wall and made the two into one new man, reconciling both to God through the cross. Gentile believers are no longer strangers but fellow-citizens and members of God’s household, a holy temple built on the apostles and prophets, with Christ as the chief cornerstone.

items.text: The Mystery Revealed to the Gentiles
For this cause I Paul, the prisoner of Christ Jesus in behalf of you Gentiles,—
if so be that ye have heard of the dispensation of that grace of God which was given me to you-ward;
how that by revelation was made known unto me the mystery, as I wrote before in few words,
whereby, when ye read, ye can perceive my understanding in the mystery of Christ;
which in other generations was not made known unto the sons of men, as it hath now been revealed unto his holy apostles and prophets in the Spirit;
to wit, that the Gentiles are fellow-heirs, and fellow-members of the body, and fellow-partakers of the promise in Christ Jesus through the gospel,
whereof I was made a minister, according to the gift of that grace of God which was given me according to the working of his power.
Unto me, who am less than the least of all saints, was this grace given, to preach unto the Gentiles the unsearchable riches of Christ;
and to make all men see what is the dispensation of the mystery which for ages hath been hid in God who created all things;
to the intent that now unto the principalities and the powers in the heavenly places might be made known through the church the manifold wisdom of God,
according to the eternal purpose which he purposed in Christ Jesus our Lord:
in whom we have boldness and access in confidence through our faith in him.
Wherefore I ask that ye may not faint at my tribulations for you, which are your glory.
Prayer to Know the Love of Christ
For this cause I bow my knees unto the Father,
from whom every family in heaven and on earth is named,
that he would grant you, according to the riches of his glory, that ye may be strengthened with power through his Spirit in the inward man;
that Christ may dwell in your hearts through faith; to the end that ye, being rooted and grounded in love,
may be strong to apprehend with all the saints what is the breadth and length and height and depth,
and to know the love of Christ which passeth knowledge, that ye may be filled unto all the fulness of God.
Now unto him that is able to do exceeding abundantly above all that we ask or think, according to the power that worketh in us,
unto him be the glory in the church and in Christ Jesus unto all generations for ever and ever. Amen.

summary.title: CHAPTER 3 IN SUMMARY
paras: Writing as “the prisoner of Christ Jesus,” Paul explains the mystery God revealed to him: through the gospel, Gentiles are fellow-heirs, fellow-members of the body and fellow-partakers of the promise in Christ. Paul calls himself “less than the least of all saints,” yet God gave him the grace to preach the unsearchable riches of Christ. Through the church, God’s manifold wisdom is now displayed even to the powers in the heavenly places, so Paul asks them not to lose heart over his sufferings.

He then bows in a second prayer. He asks that they be strengthened by the Spirit in the inner man, that Christ would dwell in their hearts through faith, and that, rooted and grounded in love, they would grasp the breadth, length, height and depth of Christ’s love, which passes knowledge. The first half of the letter closes with praise to God, who is able to do “exceeding abundantly above all that we ask or think.”

items.text: Unity and Growth in the Body
I therefore, the prisoner in the Lord, beseech you to walk worthily of the calling wherewith ye were called,
with all lowliness and meekness, with longsuffering, forbearing one another in love;
giving diligence to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.
There is one body, and one Spirit, even as also ye were called in one hope of your calling;
one Lord, one faith, one baptism,
one God and Father of all, who is over all, and through all, and in all.
But unto each one of us was the grace given according to the measure of the gift of Christ.
Wherefore he saith, When he ascended on high, he led captivity captive, And gave gifts unto men.
(Now this, He ascended, what is it but that he also descended into the lower parts of the earth?
He that descended is the same also that ascended far above all the heavens, that he might fill all things.)
And he gave some to be apostles; and some, prophets; and some, evangelists; and some, pastors and teachers;
for the perfecting of the saints, unto the work of ministering, unto the building up of the body of Christ:
till we all attain unto the unity of the faith, and of the knowledge of the Son of God, unto a fullgrown man, unto the measure of the stature of the fulness of Christ:
that we may be no longer children, tossed to and fro and carried about with every wind of doctrine, by the sleight of men, in craftiness, after the wiles of error;
but speaking truth in love, may grow up in all things into him, who is the head, even Christ;

from whom all the body fitly framed and knit together through that which every joint supplieth, according to the working in due measure of each several part, maketh the increase of the body unto the building up of itself in love.
Put Off the Old, Put On the New
This I say therefore, and testify in the Lord, that ye no longer walk as the Gentiles also walk, in the vanity of their mind,
being darkened in their understanding, alienated from the life of God, because of the ignorance that is in them, because of the hardening of their heart;
who being past feeling gave themselves up to lasciviousness, to work all uncleanness with greediness.
But ye did not so learn Christ;
if so be that ye heard him, and were taught in him, even as truth is in Jesus:
that ye put away, as concerning your former manner of life, the old man, that waxeth corrupt after the lusts of deceit;
and that ye be renewed in the spirit of your mind,
and put on the new man, that after God hath been created in righteousness and holiness of truth.
Wherefore, putting away falsehood, speak ye truth each one with his neighbor: for we are members one of another.
Be ye angry, and sin not: let not the sun go down upon your wrath:
neither give place to the devil.
Let him that stole steal no more: but rather let him labor, working with his hands the thing that is good, that he may have whereof to give to him that hath need.
Let no corrupt speech proceed out of your mouth, but such as is good for edifying as the need may be, that it may give grace to them that hear.
And grieve not the Holy Spirit of God, in whom ye were sealed unto the day of redemption.
Let all bitterness, and wrath, and anger, and clamor, and railing, be put away from you, with all malice:
and be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving each other, even as God also in Christ forgave you.

summary.title: CHAPTER 4 IN SUMMARY
paras: Here the letter turns from what God has done to how believers should live: “walk worthily of the calling wherewith ye were called.” Paul urges humility, meekness, patience and a careful guarding of the unity of the Spirit, because there is one body, one Spirit, one hope, one Lord, one faith, one baptism and one God and Father of all. The risen Christ gave gifts to the church (apostles, prophets, evangelists, pastors and teachers) to equip the saints for ministry. The goal is a body that grows up into maturity in Christ, no longer tossed by every wind of doctrine but “speaking truth in love.”

Paul then contrasts the old life with the new. Believers must no longer walk as the Gentiles do, in futile thinking and hardened hearts. They are to put off the old man, be renewed in the spirit of their minds, and put on the new man created in righteousness and holiness. He makes it practical: speak truth, be angry but do not sin, stop stealing and work so you can give, let no corrupt speech come out of your mouth, and do not grieve the Holy Spirit. Instead, be kind, tenderhearted and forgiving, “even as God also in Christ forgave you.”

items.text: Walk in Love and Light
Be ye therefore imitators of God, as beloved children;
and walk in love, even as Christ also loved you, and gave himself up for us, an offering and a sacrifice to God for an odor of a sweet smell.
But fornication, and all uncleanness, or covetousness, let it not even be named among you, as becometh saints;
nor filthiness, nor foolish talking, or jesting, which are not befitting: but rather giving of thanks.
For this ye know of a surety, that no fornicator, nor unclean person, nor covetous man, who is an idolater, hath any inheritance in the kingdom of Christ and God.
Let no man deceive you with empty words: for because of these things cometh the wrath of God upon the sons of disobedience.
Be not ye therefore partakers with them;
for ye were once darkness, but are now light in the Lord: walk as children of light
(for the fruit of the light is in all goodness and righteousness and truth),
proving what is well-pleasing unto the Lord;
and have no fellowship with the unfruitful works of darkness, but rather even reprove them;
for the things which are done by them in secret it is a shame even to speak of.
But all things when they are reproved are made manifest by the light: for everything that is made manifest is light.
Wherefore he saith, Awake, thou that sleepest, and arise from the dead, and Christ shall shine upon thee.
Look therefore carefully how ye walk, not as unwise, but as wise;
redeeming the time, because the days are evil.
Wherefore be ye not foolish, but understand what the will of the Lord is.
And be not drunken with wine, wherein is riot, but be filled with the Spirit;
speaking one to another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody with your heart to the Lord;
giving thanks always for all things in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ to God, even the Father;
subjecting yourselves one to another in the fear of Christ.
Wives and Husbands
Wives, be in subjection unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord.
For the husband is the head of the wife, as Christ also is the head of the church, being himself the saviour of the body.
But as the church is subject to Christ, so let the wives also be to their husbands in everything.
Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself up for it;
that he might sanctify it, having cleansed it by the washing of water with the word,
that he might present the church to himself a glorious church, not having spot or wrinkle or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish.
Even so ought husbands also to love their own wives as their own bodies. He that loveth his own wife loveth himself:
for no man ever hated his own flesh; but nourisheth and cherisheth it, even as Christ also the church;
because we are members of his body.
For this cause shall a man leave his father and mother, and shall cleave to his wife; and the two shall become one flesh.
This mystery is great: but I speak in regard of Christ and of the church.
Nevertheless do ye also severally love each one his own wife even as himself; and let the wife see that she fear her husband.

summary.title: CHAPTER 5 IN SUMMARY
paras: Paul calls believers to be imitators of God, as beloved children, and to walk in love just as Christ loved them and gave Himself for them. Sexual immorality, impurity, greed and coarse talk have no place among saints; thanksgiving should take their place. Once they were darkness, but now they are light in the Lord, so they must walk as children of light and expose the unfruitful works of darkness. They should walk carefully, “redeeming the time,” and rather than being drunk with wine, be filled with the Spirit. That fullness shows itself in songs, thanksgiving and submitting to one another in the fear of Christ.

Paul applies this to marriage. Wives are to be subject to their husbands as the church is to Christ. Husbands are to love their wives as Christ loved the church and gave Himself up for her, caring for them as they care for their own bodies. Paul says marriage points beyond itself to a great mystery: the union of Christ and His church.

questions.label: OBSERVE
questions.text: What does Paul say in vv. 1–14 about walking in love and walking as children of light?

questions.label: THEN
questions.text: In a Roman household where husbands held great power, how would the call for husbands to love their wives as Christ loved the church (v. 25) have sounded?

questions.label: NOW
questions.text: Paul speaks of subjecting yourselves one to another in the fear of Christ (v. 21); how might that principle reshape relationships in your home or community?

items.text: Children, Parents, Servants, Masters
Children, obey your parents in the Lord: for this is right.
Honor thy father and mother (which is the first commandment with promise),
that it may be well with thee, and thou mayest live long on the earth.
And, ye fathers, provoke not your children to wrath: but nurture them in the chastening and admonition of the Lord.
Servants, be obedient unto them that according to the flesh are your masters, with fear and trembling, in singleness of your heart, as unto Christ;
not in the way of eyeservice, as men-pleasers; but as servants of Christ, doing the will of God from the heart;
with good will doing service, as unto the Lord, and not unto men:
knowing that whatsoever good thing each one doeth, the same shall he receive again from the Lord, whether he be bond or free.
And, ye masters, do the same things unto them, and forbear threatening: knowing that he who is both their Master and yours is in heaven, and there is no respect of persons with him.
The Whole Armor of God
Finally, be strong in the Lord, and in the strength of his might.
Put on the whole armor of God, that ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil.

For our wrestling is not against flesh and blood, but against the principalities, against the powers, against the world-rulers of this darkness, against the spiritual hosts of wickedness in the heavenly places.
Wherefore take up the whole armor of God, that ye may be able to withstand in the evil day, and, having done all, to stand.
Stand therefore, having girded your loins with truth, and having put on the breastplate of righteousness,
and having shod your feet with the preparation of the gospel of peace;
withal taking up the shield of faith, wherewith ye shall be able to quench all the fiery darts of the evil one.
And take the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God:
with all prayer and supplication praying at all seasons in the Spirit, and watching thereunto in all perseverance and supplication for all the saints,
and on my behalf, that utterance may be given unto me in opening my mouth, to make known with boldness the mystery of the gospel,
for which I am an ambassador in chains; that in it I may speak boldly, as I ought to speak.
Final Greetings
But that ye also may know my affairs, how I do, Tychicus, the beloved brother and faithful minister in the Lord, shall make known to you all things:
whom I have sent unto you for this very purpose, that ye may know our state, and that he may comfort your hearts.
Peace be to the brethren, and love with faith, from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
Grace be with all them that love our Lord Jesus Christ with a love incorruptible.

summary.title: CHAPTER 6 IN SUMMARY
paras: The household instructions continue. Children are to obey and honor their parents, the first commandment with a promise, and fathers are not to provoke their children but raise them in the discipline and instruction of the Lord. Servants are to obey their earthly masters sincerely, as though serving Christ Himself. Masters must treat their servants the same way, remembering that both have the same Master in heaven, who shows no partiality.

Paul’s final charge is to be strong in the Lord. The real battle is not against flesh and blood but against spiritual forces of wickedness, so believers must take up the whole armor of God: truth, righteousness, the readiness of the gospel of peace, faith, salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God. They are to pray at all times, including for Paul, “an ambassador in chains,” that he may speak the gospel boldly. He sends Tychicus with news and closes with a blessing of peace, love, faith and grace.

wrap.title: Ephesians In Summary
paras: Ephesians falls into two halves that belong together. Chapters 1–3 tell what God has done: He chose, adopted, redeemed and sealed His people in Christ, raised them from death in sin to life by grace, and joined Jew and Gentile into one new people. Chapters 4–6 tell how that people should live: “walk worthily of the calling wherewith ye were called.” Paul never gives a command until he has first laid out the gift. Christian living, in Ephesians, is the natural response to grace already received, not a way of earning it.

Two small words carry the whole letter. The first is “in Christ” (or “in him”), which Paul uses again and again, especially in chapter 1. Every blessing, every hope and every part of the believer’s identity is found in union with Christ. The second is “walk.” Believers once walked in trespasses and sins (2:1–2). Now they walk in good works (2:10), worthily of their calling (4:1), in love (5:2), as children of light (5:8) and carefully, redeeming the time (5:15–16).

At the center of the letter is the church. Paul calls it Christ’s body (1:23), a holy temple (2:21) and Christ’s bride (5:25–32). In it the deepest division of Paul’s world, between Jew and Gentile, has been torn down at the cross. This is the “mystery” revealed to Paul: the church is meant to display God’s wisdom even to the powers in the heavenly places. That is why unity matters so much in chapter 4, and why everyday relationships at home and work matter in chapters 5 and 6.

Ephesians also speaks plainly about unseen powers. It opens with Christ seated “far above all rule, and authority, and power, and dominion” (1:21) and closes with believers standing firm against “the spiritual hosts of wickedness” (6:12) in the armor of God. For a church that came out of the Artemis cult and Ephesian magic, and that lived under Rome and its emperor worship, this was a direct word. Christ is Lord over every power they had once feared or served. The setting adds weight to all of it. Paul wrote as a prisoner in Rome, chained to a soldier, in the last quiet years before Nero turned on the Christians. Yet the letter is full of praise, not complaint. He prays twice that his readers would know the hope, the power and the love of Christ, and he breaks into worship of the God “that is able to do exceeding abundantly above all that we ask or think” (3:20). The letter’s message in one line: God in His grace has made us one in Christ, so live as one, walk in love, and stand firm in His strength.
